answer: Stake-bonded identity resists sybil attacks in an agent economy: each agent must lock a deposit before trading or attesting, so every fake identity costs real capital. Reputation accrues only through verified completed work, and misbehavior triggers slashing of the bond. Like an echo fading without renewal, a fake identity cannot persist without ongoing cost. An oasis of trust forms around agents whose bonds and work history are public, while a whisper of unverified claims carries no weight. Attackers must pay per identity and risk losing it, making large-scale fakery economically irrational.
